findings.claim: Ruling (b) changes what `cap` counts but leaves every docket case gated on 'read only from a review written in this iteration; an iteration with no new review is none' (also plan-review-design.md:136). D-40 exempts only the guard, so cap is still never read in an iteration that writes no review, which is exactly the iteration G-55 is about.
findings.failure_scenario: The arbiter keeps writing `<slug>-review.N.txt`, which FENCE_WRITE refuses. No review lands, so every iteration ends with docket `none` whatever the iteration count in `<slug>.iter.txt` says. Iteration 200 arrives with no ask and the loop fails on max_iterations: the G-55 defect still stands.

findings.claim: The ruling counts 'a line per `state` call' as writing does, but writing's `state` runs once per iteration (writing-design.md:128) and both hearings call mode `state` twice per iteration: `filing` at :302 and `ready` at :334 (spec-review-design.md:390 and :422). `docket-in` (:264, spec :347) also calls `state` outside the loop.
findings.failure_scenario: Each iteration appends 2 lines, so the count reaches CAP=200 near iteration 100. From then on every iteration asks the owner a `cap` question while 100 autonomous iterations remain, which is a stop on a non-issue (CLAUDE.md 1.4). `docket-in` adds one more line per run, so the base taken from it is off by one.

findings.claim: The new counter `gauntlet/plans/<slug>.iter.txt` matches the defense's FENCE_WRITE `gauntlet/plans/*.txt`, and FENCE_DENY covers only the review, ruling and cite files. The speccer has the same gap at spec-review-design.md:283 (`gauntlet/specs/*.txt`, with only review and ruling denied). Contract row P20 (contracts.md:81) lists no iter file, so no fence row is brought along with the ruling.
findings.failure_scenario: The defense or speccer, the agent whose spinning the cap guards against, can overwrite or truncate `<slug>.iter.txt` with an ordinary write_file. The line count then drops below CAP, the ask never fires, and the loop ends on max_iterations. Writing's file sits in `gauntlet/write/`, which no writer fence covers, so 'as writing does' does not carry over here.

findings.claim: Cap logic can live only in `.shared/rounds.py` (spec-review-design.md:514), and writing's revision hearing calls that file too (PROFILE folder `gauntlet/revisions`, writing-design.md:80). Moving iteration counting into `rounds.state` gives writing a second iteration counter and a second `cap` case. The ruling does not say which profile owns the counter.
findings.failure_scenario: stage.py docket returns rounds.docket's case first (:172). A rounds-level `cap`, counted from `gauntlet/revisions/<slug>.iter.txt`, can fire ahead of stage's own cap and go to `rounds.record` as a revision-round ruling. That file is also writable by the reviser through `gauntlet/revisions/*.txt` (writing-design.md:333).
